slides.title: Choosing for your own product
slides.lead: The report's decision framework, with the step that shows each option. Transport first, because your product decides it. Generation mode second, because it is a cost and control trade you can revisit.
slides.notes: The closing section turns the series into a decision. Two tables from the report, annotated with the steps that demonstrate each row, then the numbers this series measured, then the rules that held.

rows: How much does open-ended HTML cost against a flat spec?
nine to ten times the tokens, eight times the wall time, over three runs

every cell reproduces: OpenUI Lang 4,800 tokens against 9,122 YAML, 9,948 C1 JSON, 10,180 patches

slides.notes: These are the numbers to remember. Every one comes from a demo script in the repository, run against a real model on the recording machine. The token multiples for open-ended generation and the first-paint difference for flat maps are the two that change design decisions.

slides.title: Three rules that held across all 23 steps
bullets: **Structure before content.** Every format that streams well names the layout first and fills it later: flat maps, forward references, patches against ids. A nested document cannot paint until it closes.
**The catalog is the contract.** Prompt, validation and rendering come from one definition. Change the definition and all three change. This is what keeps declarative generation safe.
**Errors are results.** A spec that fails validation goes back to the model as text. A blocked script stays inside its iframe. The loop never ends because the agent drew something wrong.
The harness codelab ended with the same three rules for tools. They hold for interfaces too.
slides.takeaway: Models are commodities. The harness is the product. The interface is where the product meets the user.
slides.notes: Close on the rules. They are the same shape as the harness codelab's rules, which is the point: an interface layer is a harness concern. If a reader remembers one slide, it should be this one.

slides.title: Run it, then change it
bullets: `git clone https://github.com/dlmastery/simple-coding-harness` and open `genui/README.md`: the written codelab with every snippet verified and every screenshot.
Start with `genui/01_foundations/step_01_static_components`: `python demo.py` records a run and a screenshot in under a minute.
Each README ends with a checkpoint: change the catalog, watch the prompt change; remove a prompt rule, watch the token count move.
The harness codelab in the repository root is the other half: the loop, tools, permissions, sandbox, sessions, and the same harness on TrueForge.
The State of Generative UI report is the map this series follows; the step READMEs cite the specification or library each one uses.
